samples.target:
The plot shows clear bimodal clustering with a visible gap
between the two groups, with the first cluster in the lower-left region
and the second cluster in the upper-right region. A successful submission accurately describes that
there are two distinct clusters or groups in the data, or that the data shows bimodal
clustering, or that points form two separated groups, or that there is a clear gap between
two populations. Submissions may note the approximate locations of the clusters or describe
them as distinct clouds of points.

messages.content:
create a scatterplot with the df dataset.
put `x_coord` on the x-axis and `y_coord` on the y-axis. briefly describe what you observe. The data already exists in your environment.

arguments.code:
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(df, aes(x = x_coord, y = y_coord)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "#2C7FB8") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#F03B20") +
  labs(
    title = "Scatterplot of x_coord vs y_coord",
    x = "x_coord",
    y = "y_coord"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

content.text:
Observations:
- The points form two clearly separated clusters: one at lower x and y values and another at higher x and y values.
- There’s an overall strong positive trend (upward red line), largely driven by the separation between clusters.
- Within each cluster the x–y relationship looks relatively weak, and the upper cluster shows a bit more spread.
- No major outliers are evident. If these are different groups, consider fitting lines per group or adding a grouping variable.

- IQRs and overall spreads are similar across states, so variability doesn’t differ much.
- A few points fall outside the boxes, but nothing looks like an extreme outlier. Overall, differences between states appear modest.

arguments.code:
library(ggplot2)

arguments.code:
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red", linewidth = 0.9) +
  labs(
    x = "x", y = "y",
    title = paste0(
      "Trend: ",
      ifelse(
        abs(coef(lm(y ~ x, data = df))[2]) < 1e-8, "None",
        ifelse(coef(lm(y ~ x, data = df))[2] > 0, "Positive", "Negative")
      ),
      " | Slope = ", signif(coef(lm(y ~ x, data = df))[2], 3),
      " | R² = ", signif(summary(lm(y ~ x, data = df))$r.squared, 3)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

arguments.code:

  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "#2b8cbe") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#d95f0e", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot")
